totals.enlisted_presence_note: All 51 enlisted men on the 31 May roll are taken as at Chicago on 14 Aug: no discharge, desertion or detachment is recorded after 31 May and Quaife (App. IX) sees 'no reason to suppose that there was any alteration in this number'. 31 are named in a battle/captivity source; 20 rest on the roll alone. Contemporary counts differ: Heald's report 54 regulars (probably including himself); Helm 52 privates and musicians plus 4 officers; the June quarterly/inspection returns 54; Quaife concludes 55 but allows one may have been absent.
totals.children_note: 18 per Woodward (from Heald and Griffith) and Quaife; Helm's list reads 15 in Quaife's transcription and 18 in Gordon's. 12 killed (Heald) or 13 (Helm); 6 survived the battle, one (Needs) then died. 11 children are individually identified in this file (Cicely's son; David and Susan Simmons; the Needs child; the Holt child (probable); Isabella Cooper, the Burns infant and two unnamed Burns/Cooper children; the Lee girl and the Lee infant); 7 are unidentified, most likely further Lee, Burns, Holt or Needs children. Excluded: the Healds' stillborn son (died 4 May 1812), Mrs. Corbin's unborn child, and Peter Bell (disputed).
totals.militia_note: 15 enrolled by Heald after the 6 April murders; 3 (two "half-breeds" and a Frenchman) deserted within days. Named: Thomas Burns (sergeant) and his stepson Joseph or James Cooper (certain); Lee and Lee's son (probable); Louis Fettle and Pierre LeClaire (Quaife's conjectures). At least 6 remain unnamed.
totals.whole_party_formula: 55 regulars + 12 militia + 9 women + 18 children + John Kinzie + William Wells (Miami escort not counted); Woodward counted 93 (54 military + 12 citizens + 9 + 18).

notes:
Sources and method: Quaife 1913 Appendix VIII (the 31 May 1812 roll from the Heald Papers) is the spine; each man's presence is graded 'present' only where a battle, captivity or ransom source names him (Helm's 1814 list, Woodward to Proctor 7 Oct 1812, Niles' Register 4 Jun 1814, Forsyth's letters, Heald's Journal/report, Wau-Bun incidents); otherwise 'probably_present' from the roll plus Quaife's elimination in Appendix IX. Fates are Quaife's App. IX table, which he says rests partly on 'inference and deduction' (the five tortured men, the five unrecorded returns). Line numbers are of the local plain-text files named in each locator; printed pages are given where the source carries them (Quaife and Kirkland by chapter/appendix start pages; the Gutenberg texts carry no page markers).

Gaps: (1) No source says where any soldier or family lived inside or outside the fort; all residence assignments except the commanding officer's quarters are reconstructed. After the 6 April alarm the Kinzies moved into the fort and the other civilians fortified Jouett's former agency house (Quaife ch. X; Wau-Bun ch. XVIII); whether they were still there on 14 Aug is not recorded. (2) First names are missing for every soldier's wife except Susan (Millhouse) Simmons (family narrative only), and for Lee. (3) Only one muster roll for 1812 survives; ages appear for none of the enlisted men except Kennison's own (doubtful) claim. (4) Andreas 1884 was not usefully searchable (its OCR index returned nothing relevant); Wentworth's Early Chicago (Dec 1810 roll, Edwards letter) was used only through Kirkland and Quaife. The Heald 'tabular statement' and 'summary statement concerning the women' (Draper Coll.) are known only through Quaife.

Discrepancies to carry, not resolve: Wells's arrival 13 Aug with ~30 Miamis (Heald), 12 Aug with 27 (Helm), 14 Aug with 15 (Wau-Bun). Destruction of arms/liquor: night of 13th (Helm, Wau-Bun), 14th (Heald). Wau-Bun's 'veteran of seventy winters' who fell first is unidentified (Kennison, by his own claimed age about 76, is held by Quaife to have survived). Thomas Forth's term expired 6 July 1812 with no re-enlistment shown. Helm's 'Nathan Hurt ... Deserted' may be Hunt or Hurtt. Mrs. Burns's death: about 1823 (Edwards via Quaife) vs about 1832 (Edwards 1881 letter via Kirkland). Kirkland misidentifies the scalped girl's father as surgeon's mate John Cooper; Quaife's reading (children of Mrs. Burns's first marriage) is followed.

Men on the Dec 1810 roll but not the 1812 roll (Glass, Rickman, Ashbrook, Burke, Berry, Best, Chapman, S. and J. Clark, Leonard, Loy, R. Miller, McGowan, Mabury, Moyan, P. Smith, Waggoner) were discharged or transferred; Wau-Bun says the outside population was 'a few discharged soldiers and some families of half-breeds', so some could be among the unnamed militia, but nothing names them in 1812. Ronan's 12 Nov 1811 whiskey order lists 'Keamble (?)' and 'Burman', who are on neither roll. Surgeon's mate John Cooper (resigned 1810/11) and Matthew Irwin (factor, left 5 July 1812) were not present.

Wells and the Miami escort are another researcher's: Heald report quote is on heald_nathan_1812. Kinzie household (incl. Margaret Helm's mother) also belongs to the civilian census; Margaret Helm is kept here as an officer's wife.

Language: quotes are verbatim and carry 1812-1913 usage ('savages', 'squaw', 'half-breed', 'negro'); keep them in provenance fields, paraphrase in any displayed caption.
